title: Generic fibre dimension persists on a nonempty open
statement: Let $f:X\to Y$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme]. Assume the underlying space of $Y$ is irreducible (nonempty and not the union of two proper closed subsets) with generic point $\eta$ [def-sc-generic-point], and that $f$ is of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. If the scheme-theoretic generic fibre $X_{\eta}$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] has topological Krull dimension [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension] $n\ge0$, then there exists a nonempty open subset $V\subseteq Y$ such that every fibre $X_y$ for $y\in V$ has topological Krull dimension exactly $n$.
